subject: Performance SLO: context window & latency follow-up (FinCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: context window & latency follow-up (FinCo)

Hi Sarah / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of requirements (as we captured them):
- Workload: document summarization + question-answering inside FinCo's customer portal.
- Typical input context: ~6,000 tokens (extracted document + metadata).
- Max context observed / required: up to 12,000 tokens in peak cases.
- Expected output: 400–1,000 tokens per request (usually ~700).
- Streaming: you want partial tokens streamed to the UI as they're generated (WebSocket ok).
- Throughput & concurrency targets: baseline 15 req/s, peak concurrency ~50 simultaneous sessions.
- Latency SLO: target P95 <= 1.0s for typical requests; acceptable up to 1.5s for very large contexts but would prefer <800ms for quick flows.

Key open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Are you willing to consider an approach that chunks + retrieves (embedding index) vs. single-pass large-context generation for the worst-case 12k inputs?
2) Do you need strong cross-request KV cache (i.e., session-level attention cache) or are requests mostly idempotent/standalone?
3) Any hard constraints on model family (open models ok) or GPU types?

What we'll do next:
- Share an initial SLO matrix and configuration options (will include estimated P95 numbers across model choices, quantization, and batching).
- Propose two pilot configs: (A) single-pass large-context optimized model (quantized, big-GPU); (B) retrieval/chunking with smaller context window + embedding index for tighter latency.
- Schedule technical deep-dive to review sample traces and agree pilot metrics.

I've looped in Dev and Vivek for the technical estimates — Vivek, Dev: can you confirm the rough P95 numbers we discussed for 6k vs 12k windows and prepare the SLO matrix?

Next step for FinCo: please send a small sample of representative traces or sample documents (we'll redact as needed) and confirm WebSocket streaming is acceptable.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
From: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@finco.com>

Cc: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finco.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: context window & latency follow-up (FinCo)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We can accept P95 up to ~1.5s for the absolute worst-case (12k token) calls if that's materially hard to achieve, but uniform responses under 1s are ideal.
- WebSocket streaming is fine for the UI; low-latency partial token updates are preferred.
- For chunking vs single-pass: our product team prefers single-pass where possible (simpler UX), but they're open to a hybrid approach if it guarantees latency and better relevancy.

I attached our current usage estimate CSV (finco-usage-estimates.csv) showing expected monthly active users and request distribution by doc size.

We're available for the deep-dive next week (Mar 22–24 window).

Regards,
Rajesh
VP Product, FinCo

Attachment: finco-usage-estimates.csv (stub - CSV with traffic buckets)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: context window & latency follow-up (FinCo)

Looping in technical thoughts / quick sanity checks: 

Marissa / Dev —
Quick clarifying Qs for the FinCo team (if you can confirm to Rajesh/Sarah):
- Is deterministic output ordering important, or can we use retrieval + chunked prompting with reranking? This matters for small-window fallbacks.
- Do they expect session affinity (i.e., KV cache across multi-turn sessions)? That influences memory footprints.

Rough numbers from our runtime benchmarks (ballpark for a modern 8-bit quantized open model):
- 6k token context + 700 token output (single-pass, no batching): P95 ~ 700–950 ms on an NVIDIA H100-class instance with optimized kernels.
- 12k token context + 1k output (single-pass, heavy): P95 ~ 1.2–1.6 s depending on concurrency and whether we can stream partial tokens as they're decoded.
- If you move to chunking + retrieval (keep model context to ~2–4k tokens), typical P95 drops < 600–800 ms and scales much better at concurrency 50+.

Tradeoffs / recommendations:
- If FinCo wants single-pass for UX simplicity, recommend quantized 16/8-bit model on large-GPU pool with streaming enabled and prefix caching where possible. Plan fallback to a retrieval path for >10k inputs.
- For strict latency SLO <800 ms at concurrency 50, retrieval + chunking is the safer path.

Next steps I suggest we include in the SLO matrix: expected P95/P99, cost per 1M tokens, and recommended batching settings (max batch size, request-timeout) and streaming buffer sizes. I'll draft these with Dev and attach the matrix.

-Vivek
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@finco.com>, Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: SLO matrix & pilot configurations — FinCo

Hi Rajesh / Sarah —

Following up with the SLO matrix and two recommended pilot configs. Attachment: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (stub) — contains estimated latency, throughput, and cost rows for each model/config. Summary below: 

Pilot A — Single-pass large-context (UX-first)
- Model: Open LLM-optimized 70B (8-bit quantized)
- HW: H100-class GPU pool, dedicated instances
- Typical P95 (6k ctx + 700 out): ~800 ms
- Worst-case P95 (12k + 1k): ~1.3 s
- Concurrency: tested at 50 concurrent sessions with auto-scaling bump for peaks
- Streaming: enabled (WebSocket) — partial tokens emitted as they decode
- Notes: higher cost, simpler UX, fallback to chunking for extreme docs

Pilot B — Retrieval + chunking (latency-first)
- Model: Open 13B (8-bit) for final generation + embedding index for retrieval
- HW: mixed GPU pool (A10/H100) — lower per-token cost
- Typical P95: <600 ms (for 2–4k effective context)
- Worst-case P95: <900 ms (includes retrieval time)
- Concurrency: scales to 100+ with lower unit cost
- Notes: additional infra for embeddings/indexing, slightly more complex UX (but can be abstracted client-side)

Requested next items from FinCo: 
- Sample traces (we received the CSV, thank you) — if you can also provide 10 representative example docs, that'll help us calibrate retrieval chunk sizes.
- Confirm whether session KV caching is required.
- Agree pilot success criteria: target P95 and cost per request for 30-day pilot.

I've attached the SLO matrix and added a link to a shared deep-dive doc here: https://drive.google.com/example-finco-deepdive.

If this looks good we'll set up a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive week of Mar 22–24 and bring in infra + runtime engineering to finalize configs.

Thanks — Dev

Attachment: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (stub - contains benchmark rows and cost estimates)
From: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO: context window & latency follow-up (FinCo)

Thanks everyone — this is super helpful.

We're happy to proceed with a pilot. A few confirmations:
- WebSocket streaming is fine.
- We'll prioritize the retrieval + chunking pilot (Pilot B) for latency guarantees, but keep the single-pass option as a backup for specific workflows.
- I'll upload 10 representative docs to the Drive link and confirm whether session-level KV cache is required (expectation: not required for first pilot).
- Deep-dive: Mar 23rd, 10:00–11:30 PT works for our engineers.

See you then — Rajesh
